questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
Can a super PAC give $10,000 directly to a House candidate's campaign?
questions.why: Super PACs can raise unlimited money but can't give to candidates or coordinate with them. They can only spend independently.

questions.prompt: In the final 60 days, who pays less for the same TV spot?
questions.why: Stations must sell candidates airtime at the lowest unit charge. Outside groups pay market rates, which climb near Election Day.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Democrats have spent $2.0M in IN's 5th District House race. Are Democrats playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Democrats here is offense.

questions.prompt: NO GOING BACK PAC INC. (a super PAC) has spent $506K in OH's 15th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: AB PAC (a super PAC) has spent $366K in NC's 9th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: How often do House and Senate campaigns file their regular reports in an election year?
questions.why: Candidate committees file quarterly, plus 12 days before and 30 days after each election. Monthly filing is only an option for PACs and parties.

questions.prompt: In NH's 1st District House race, outside money favors Democrats by $326K. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Republican leads fundraising by $2.0M.
